# Use architecture-diagrams

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Generate architecture diagrams (Mermaid, PlantUML, C4) from a written description of a system. Supports AWS/Azure/GCP cloud topologies, microservice landscapes, sequence flows, container diagrams, and ER models.

**Reach for it when** Use whenever the user asks for an architecture diagram, system sketch, flow diagram, or visualization of a design.

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install architecture-diagrams                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install architecture-diagrams --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install architecture-diagrams --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Solution architect pack: [`--pack solution-architect`](../packs/use-the-solution-architect-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "Draw an architecture diagram for this system"
- "Generate a Mermaid diagram of these services"
- "Create a C4 container diagram from this description"
- "Diagram the sequence flow I just described"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "Reverse-engineer the architecture from our Terraform and repo"
- "Read the frames in our Figma file"
- "Threat model this design"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use architecture-diagrams".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Fit on one screen.** If you have more than ~15 nodes, split into two diagrams (e.g., "Context" and "Container") rather than cramming everything in.
- **Show direction of data flow,** not just connections. Arrows should mean something.
- **Label every arrow** that crosses a trust boundary or a network hop.
- **Use subgraphs / groups** to make zones explicit (VPC, public/private subnets, account boundaries, on-prem vs cloud).
- **Be valid syntax.** Mentally trace through the Mermaid/PlantUML once before responding. Common breakers: unescaped `(` `)` `<` `>` inside labels, missing `end` for subgraphs, mixing graph types.
